reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational principles of behavior are rooted in the amplification of reaction potential through positive habit tendencies. This process is mediated by drive stimuli (S_p), which activate receptors and initiate physiological responses. Endocrine substances act as modulators, lowering thresholds for specific effectors while simultaneously enhancing overall effector responsiveness—this dual role mirrors the Freudian concept of libido. The generalized facilitation of action across all effectors implies a shared motivational substrate that can be interpreted as a scalar field influencing behavioral dynamics. When one primary drive fades, residual motivation persists due to the lingering effects of endocrine modulation, explaining sustained but limited habitual behavior. This mechanism supports sublimation, wherein sexual or other drives redirect toward non-instinctual goals. The interplay between differential drive stimuli enables discrimination in complex behavioral contexts, suggesting that stimulus patterning mediates choice among competing motivations. These insights form the basis for constructing probabilistic models of motivation and action selection within GSI and GSE frameworks.
